#634. 22 fish shipped from Massachusetts to Georgia—very carefully

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (428 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci

22 fish shipped from Massachusetts to Georgia—very carefully

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that boston’s Latest England Aquarium recently shipped a very important package.
  • It has been revealed that “By working together, we are able to raise more fish, and develop aquaculture practices to successfully raise more species, including some that have never been raised before, like copper/glassy sweepers, blue chromis, and brown chromis,” Monika Schmück, manager of sustainability in the fishes department at the Newly introduced England Aquarium, tells Popular Science.
  • According to recent reports, sharing is caring, even amongst aquariums.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that boston’s Latest England Aquarium recently shipped a very important package. But it wasn’t exactly an early Christmas gift. The team shipped 22 lookdown fish across the country via air transport. And they’re not the only institution that routinely packs fishes up and sends them elsewhere. The NEA are part of a group of aquariums where each member specializes in raising certain species on behalf of the entire group. They then send the fish to the other member aquariums.

It has been revealed that “By working together, we are able to raise more fish, and develop aquaculture practices to successfully raise more species, including some that have never been raised before, like copper/glassy sweepers, blue chromis, and brown chromis,” Monika Schmück, manager of sustainability in the fishes department at the Newly introduced England Aquarium, tells Popular Science. “We typically raise 500-1000 fish annually and distribute them to over 15 institutions on average each year.”.

According to recent reports, sharing is caring, even amongst aquariums. When it comes time for the fish’s journey, the team needs to decide whether to use air or ground transport. To do this, they consider factors including external temperature, the weight of the shipment, and access to an airport at the destination. Depending on the time of the year, cargo holding and ground transport trucks can experience extreme temperatures, Schmück points out.

If it’s a large shipment, the New England Aquarium usually goes for air cargo, whereas smaller shipments are easier to deliver with ground transportation. Overall, ground transportation is the easiest strategy because it doesn’t have to take into account the location of airports.

Industry observers note that on a smaller scale, moving a fish isn’t as easy as sticking a cat into a crate. In terms of the container in which the animal will travel, the biggest consideration is the size of said animal, which determines how much water it needs.

“Since fish must be transported in water, and water is heavy, the design of a fish transport first must address how to safely move the required volume of water to keep the fish safe and secure during the process,” Schmück explains.

Industry observers note that ultimately, the fundamentals of fish transport are mostly consistent no matter the species. Experts need to make sure that the water chemistry is good during the entire trip and that other environmental conditions are appropriate for the traveling species and remain stable.

#631. Industry News: ‘Vibe coding’ is risky: Here’s why and what to do about it

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (864 w)
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Popsci

Industry News: ‘Vibe coding’ is risky: Here’s why and what to do about it

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to rapid advances in AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, “vibe coding” is very much a possibility for anyone: Just use natural language to explain what you want a program to do, and the AI will put it together for you.
  • Recent findings suggest that this has led non-programmers to quickly create their own sites and apps, and you’ll find a multitude of examples online.
  • According to recent reports, vibe-coding gadgets can lead to some impressive demonstrations of AI’s current capabilities, but is it wise to try it at home on the devices you use every day?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to rapid advances in AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, “vibe coding” is very much a possibility for anyone: Just use natural language to explain what you want a program to do, and the AI will put it together for you.

Recent findings suggest that this has led non-programmers to quickly create their own sites and apps, and you’ll find a multitude of examples online. Vibe coding has extended to hardware too—whether it’s people hacking into their 1994 Cherokee Jeep or repurposing an Amazon Kindle.

According to recent reports, vibe-coding gadgets can lead to some impressive demonstrations of AI’s current capabilities, but is it wise to try it at home on the devices you use every day? Probably not, and we’ll explain why here.

If you’ve never used an AI app to vibe code—or used an AI app at all—then you might be wondering what all the talk about vibe coding actually means. It’s the widely used, informal term for prompting an AI chatbot to create a program: Maybe you want a phone app to track your exercise, for example, or a simple game you can play in your browser.

Sources indicate that as long as your ambitions aren’t too grand—you’re not going to get GTA VI out of this anytime soon—your AI engine of choice will produce a slick, usable, custom-made app for you within a few minutes. If there are any bugs or concerns (and there often are), then you can use follow-up prompts to get rid of them.

According to recent reports, while the end results might need a bit of finessing and don’t match up to what a team of professional software developers can do, it’s incredible to think that AI now enables anyone to write apps of their own, no manual coding required. Need a registration website for your sports club or an app to track trains at your local station? Just ask for it.

That’s not to say there aren’t downsides to vibe coding, though, which we’ll get to next. AI code isn’t always the most reliable or efficient, and you need to be aware of its limitations—and put safeguards in place to make sure there’s no danger of vibe-coded apps causing concerns for other hardware and software.

As TechCrunch reports, television sets are common targets for some vibe-coded tinkering. Users are using code produced by AI apps to simplify the app launchers, take out sponsored content and advertising, and turn off some of the aggressive tracking features that come with modern-day TVs, for example.

Here’s the problem: While the AI app developers don’t often mention it, AI code often comes with bugs and unintended consequences attached, and if you don’t understand what you’re coding, then you can’t fix it. That’s not so much of an issue if you’re trying to get a custom soccer score tracker running in your browser, but if you’re suddenly bricking your main TV, then that is a problem.

Recent findings suggest that the operating systems on TVs—as well as tablets, laptops, speakers, fridges, and other gadgets—can be complex, and AIs will often guess at what the right approach is if they don’t know for sure. You risk breaking key functionality, creating fresh bugs while trying to fix existing ones, and leaving security vulnerabilities open that hackers can target.

According to recent reports, of course it’s easy to see the appeal of an ad-free TV that runs faster than before, but is it worth opening up your television set to malware? Or not being able to use the Netflix app for reasons you can’t fathom? Or one day finding that it’s stuck in an endless loop between shutting down and powering up? These are the risks of vibe coding.

Sources indicate that different categories of devices work in different ways, but you’ll often find that there are more reliable ways of customizing your hardware than relying on something you’ve vibe-coded yourself. When it comes to TVs, for example, there are often alternative launchers available, such as Projectivy Launcher for Google TV models, which is ad-free and offers a ton of customization options.

For routers, there’s something like OpenWrt, which is built and maintained by a large enthusiast community. It lets you do all sorts of things with compatible routers, including blocking ads and trackers, customizing which devices can access the network and when, monitoring bandwidth, and integrating a VPN at the router level.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking to do more with your smart home devices, then Home Assistant is definitely worth a look. The popular alternative smart home system management software gives you much more control over your devices and what you can do with them than the comparable apps offered by Amazon, Google, and Apple.

It has been revealed that you’re still putting your faith in third-party code that you haven’t personally written—but these projects are managed by capable software developers and backed by substantial user communities that monitor concerns like security and compatibility. When it comes to keeping your gadgets usable, they’re the safer bet.

#626. Battery patents: Solid-state filings surpass lithium-ion to hit record high

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (465 w)
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pv-magazine

Battery patents: Solid-state filings surpass lithium-ion to hit record high

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (465 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pv-magazine

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that global patent filings for solid-state batteries reached a record 2,230 in 2024, up 16% from 2023.
  • In contrast, lithium-ion battery patents across chemistries and applications fell nearly 15% to 2,092, with the data clerly showing consecutive years of declines.
  • South Korea overtook Japan to lead global solid-state filings in 2024, posting 873 applications compared to Japan’s 605.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that global patent filings for solid-state batteries reached a record 2,230 in 2024, up 16% from 2023. That’s according to the sixth annual Inside Green Innovation: Progress Report by intellectual property firm Appleyard Lees, which tracks patent filings across domains including food, such as cultivated meat, recycling, and fusion energy.

In contrast, lithium-ion battery patents across chemistries and applications fell nearly 15% to 2,092, with the data clerly showing consecutive years of declines. The report tracks complete public patent data through December 31, 2024, given delays across regions in visibility of applications.

South Korea overtook Japan to lead global solid-state filings in 2024, posting 873 applications compared to Japan’s 605. Japan had held the top spot every year through 2023, but South Korea’s nearly 50% year-on-year surge, driven largely by Samsung SDI, shifted the balance. Samsung SDI nearly doubled its solid-state filings from 165 to 325, more than twice Toyota’s combined total of 144.

China ranked third in solid-state priority filings with 217, more than doubling its output since 2022, while Europe reached a record 177 filings. South Korea also maintained the lead in conventional lithium-ion filings, which nearly doubled from 441 in 2020 to 833 in 2024.

Chris Mason, Partner at Appleyard Lees, stated solid-state electrolytes highlighted the strongest growth in the data, while lithium-ion technologies “appear to be consolidating, with filing numbers decreasing for a second consecutive year.”.

In part, this reflections the maturing and commercialized supply chain around LFP cells for stationary energy storage. Patent volume is generally a lagging indicator of R&D spend.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, sodium-ion patent activity cooled after a record 2023, dropping 29% from 555 filings to 392, though still outpacing any year prior to 2022. European organizations filed a record 76 sodium-ion patents in 2024, taking second place behind China.

Appleyard Lees noted “flow battery filings remain on a plateau” that began in 2016, even as grid-scale storage is deployed at record rates.

Though not strictly related to energy storage, the annual coverage of fusion energy always reveals interesting trends in technology development. The report notes, quote:.

“Fusion is becoming a platform technology sector, as much as an energy sector, generating intellectual property with relevance far beyond future fusion power plants.

According to recent reports, “Fusion research is inherently multidisciplinary. Delivering practical fusion energy requires breakthroughs across plasma physics, superconducting materials, advanced manufacturing, control systems, isotope handling, cryogenics and numerous other technical fields. Many of these technologies have applications in markets that are already established and considerably closer to commercial deployment than fusion power itself.”.

“As a result, the fusion innovation landscape represents a rich source of intellectual property, licensing opportunities and potential spin-outs with relevance across sectors including semiconductors, healthcare, aerospace, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing.”.

#624. Spain approves new data center rules requiring 80% renewable electricity

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (767 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pv-magazine

Spain approves new data center rules requiring 80% renewable electricity

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (767 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pv-magazine

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Spanish government approved a royal decree on Nov.
  • Third Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Ecological Transition Sara Aagesen confirmed the measures following the cabinet meeting.
  • It has been revealed that the regulation comes amid rapid growth in electricity demand from data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Spanish government approved a royal decree on Nov. 20 establishing energy sustainability, environmental, resilience and digital sovereignty requirements for data centers. The Council of Ministers also approved the country’s electricity transmission network development plan through 2030, which was presented last week.

Third Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Ecological Transition Sara Aagesen confirmed the measures following the cabinet meeting.

It has been revealed that the regulation comes amid rapid growth in electricity demand from data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure. According to Aagesen, data center projects have secured grid access permits for 15 GW of capacity, including 6 GW on the transmission network and 9 GW on distribution networks. This represents nearly 40% of Spain’s peak electricity demand, while a further 20 GW of capacity is awaiting grid access.

These figures significantly exceed the projections in Spain’s 2024 Artificial Intelligence Strategy, which anticipated less than 4 GW of data center electricity demand by 2030.

According to recent reports, the government had already raised concerns about the potential impact of large-scale data center development on electricity demand, grid capacity and renewable energy deployment. In August, it proposed requiring data centers to source at least 80% of their electricity from additional renewable generation.

The approved decree introduces several changes to the initial proposal published in August, including a higher capacity threshold for the main requirements.

The revised framework targets data centers with grid access capacity of at least 10 MW, up from the 1 MW threshold initially proposed. It establishes requirements covering renewable electricity procurement, energy and water efficiency, grid flexibility, resilience and digital sovereignty.

Data centers must demonstrate that at least 80% of their annual electricity consumption is covered by on-site renewable generation or long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) with fresh renewable energy facilities.

Sources indicate that the decree also introduces hourly matching requirements between electricity consumption and renewable generation, with a phased implementation period extending to 2032. Eligible facilities can follow a transitional compliance pathway, subject to conditions including participation in demand reduction mechanisms.

According to recent reports, the regulation requires qualifying facilities to meet class A standards under the European classification systems for power usage effectiveness (PUE) and water usage effectiveness (WUE). Energy efficiency requirements will also take account of regional climatic conditions.

For water consumption, the government has established a target of 0.1 liters per kWh to achieve the highest efficiency classification.

The decree also links grid access and connection rights to compliance with the newly introduced requirements. Data centers may be required to reduce electricity demand or disconnect loads during periods of grid congestion or system stress.

Aagesen described Spain as a pioneer in regulating the energy and environmental impact of data centers.

The government estimates that, without the regulation, the expansion of data centers could add €5 billion annually to electricity costs and increase electricity bills for industrial consumers by 25%.

The measures come as Spain faces growing pressure to accommodate fresh electricity demand while managing grid constraints. The country has also been examining grid congestion and renewable energy curtailment risks as solar and other renewable energy capacity expands.

Alongside the data center decree, the Council of Ministers approved an updated electricity transmission network development plan through 2030, with planned investment of €17.14 billion ($18.82 billion).

The strategy allocates grid capacity to accommodate 47.4 GW of upcoming electricity demand, including 14.9 GW for industry, 12.4 GW for renewable hydrogen, 9.3 GW for data centers and 6 GW for residential and urban development.

It also includes approximately 6,707 km of new transmission lines, upgrades to increase capacity across 8,164 km of existing lines, and 193 substations.

Industry observers note that the investment represents a substantial increase over earlier proposals. In September, Spain raised planned grid investment above €17 billion and unveiled a capacity market to support generation, energy storage and demand-side flexibility.

The expansion of transmission infrastructure is intended to support the electrification of industry, renewable hydrogen production and other emerging sources of electricity demand, while facilitating the integration of additional renewable energy capacity.

Spain’s growing electricity demand has become an increasingly important factor in renewable energy development. According to figures published by Spanish solar association UNEF, the country had 71.5 GW of demand connection capacity either granted or included in grid planning through 2030, with a further 24 GW of pending requests.

The approval of the data center decree and transmission network initiative establishes a upcoming regulatory and infrastructure framework for accommodating electricity demand from AI infrastructure and other energy-intensive activities, while linking new data center development to renewable generation and grid flexibility requirements.

#623. Unigrid looks to fill gaps in lithium-ion storage with effective sodium-ion alternatives

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (750 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pv-magazine

Unigrid looks to fill gaps in lithium-ion storage with effective sodium-ion alternatives

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pv-magazine

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • San Diego-based Unigrid is hoping to make sodium-ion a household name.
  • Unigrid CEO Darren Tan told pv magazine USA that while there are many categories in which lithium ion does well, sodium-ion battery chemistries have advantages in crucial market segments.
  • Industry observers note that “You’ve got better safety,” Tan said, indicating sodium-ion chemistries are not flammable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

San Diego-based Unigrid is hoping to make sodium-ion a household name. The firm’s development team grew out of research centered on the University of California, San Diego, with the goal of providing battery storage technology to serve the markets where lithium-ion is not as suitable.

Unigrid CEO Darren Tan told pv magazine USA that while there are many categories in which lithium ion does well, sodium-ion battery chemistries have advantages in crucial market segments.

Industry observers note that “You’ve got better safety,” Tan said, indicating sodium-ion chemistries are not flammable. “You’ve got extremely long cycle and calendar life. Sodium just doesn’t die. Also, sodium chemistries have great thermal tolerance; they don’t care how hot it is in summer or how cold it is winter. The biggest disadvantage of the batteries is that they are heavier and take up a little more space.”.

The company indicates its 48V Na+ Casa series batteries, which are positioned for commercial and residential storage, have a discharge temperature range of about -100°F to +140°F and will charge down to about -68°F. They are UN38.3 certified and tested to UL 9540A standards at the cell level. The fire resistance of sodium-ion chemistries makes the suitable for deployment indoors, such as in hospitals or multi-unit housing.

At the same time, residential and commercial storage remains dominated by lithium-ion battery makers that are well ensconced with recognized brands with ever-increasing track records.

While there are examples of alternate chemistries and technologies, such as flow batteries, making inroads in the market, these suppliers face an uphill climb.

It is tempting, Tan indicates, to lump battery storage into a single category, but in reality, it is many, many vertical market segments. Lithium-ion chemistries, he concedes, have come to dominate the midrange endurance needs, from two to about six hours. Moreover, they are favored in many applications, from portable devices, to vehicles to grid-connected BESS. One aspect of this dominance is that suppliers and developers using them have ready access to financing.

In a recent development, lithium-ion solutions are bankable, even standard, which industry analysts have pointed out may deter the development and deployment of more appropriate technologies in key markets. At the same time, Tan claims sodium-ion is starting to get its strides in certain sectors, for example the short duration space.

For many years, there was no real demand to fill the gap between very short-duration – minutes or even seconds – applications provided by supercapacitors and the mid-range provided by batteries. However, Tan says, the advent of AI began producing strains on the grid, with demand moving from traditional arbitrage into things like ancillary services.

In a recent development, “You’ve got to service things like demand response,” Tan remarked. “You’ve got to provide capacity for uninterruptible loads; you’ve got to provide short demand charges based on load shifting. And lithium-ion is not great for that kind of high-power quick response. It also doesn’t like multiple cycles. Short-duration storage in data centers may need to cycle 10, 20 times a day, especially if you’re looking at an AI model training context.”.

According to Tan, the prevailing solution has been to use lithium-titanate oxide (LTO) batteries, which have better cycling performance, charge and discharge rates, and operational temperature ranges than lithium-ion. LTO is also much more expensive, coming in at 20 times the cost of lithium-ion.

In a recent development, “Sodium-ion checks all the boxes,” Tan noted. “High power, very long cycle life, wide temperature ranges so you don’t have to cool it, and it’s also very safe. And we can compete on price.”.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Tan mentioned the most significant challenges Unigrid faces with its sodium-ion batteries are achieving the third-party testing benchmarks and winning necessary regulatory certification for widespread deployment in the U.S. Lithium-ion BESS suppliers have already cleared many of these hurdles. Tan states Unigrid is looking to its installations in Europe and other parts of the world to support its plans for succeeding in the U.S. market. He is hopeful that increasing demand and the rising price of diesel and other fuels will prompt developers – and financiers – to take a good look at sodium-ion batteries.

A recent study by Wood Mackenzie identifies sodium-ion batteries as the most promising emerging alternative to lithium-based technologies for stationary energy storage. Manufacturers are expected to achieve cell-level cost parity with lithium iron phosphate batteries by late 2026, while parity at the module and system levels is not expected until after 2030.

#620. Celebrating men, challenging stereotypes, building a stronger energy future together

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1407 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pv-magazine

Celebrating men, challenging stereotypes, building a stronger energy future together

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pv-magazine

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that someone once asked me why I had decided to create a women’s network in the solar industry.
  • According to recent reports, on International Men’s Day, Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) wants to celebrate the men across our solar, energy storage and wider energy transition industries.
  • Our industry has something extraordinary in common: a purpose that goes far beyond individual careers or commercial success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that someone once asked me why I had decided to create a women’s network in the solar industry. My answer was simple: “Because our industry is full of good men who already want to change the world, and I couldn’t think of better ground on which to build a network that could help us change it together.”.

According to recent reports, on International Men’s Day, Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) wants to celebrate the men across our solar, energy storage and wider energy transition industries. The men who recognise talent beyond gender, challenge stereotypes, encourage others to grow and understand that creating a more inclusive industry is a shared responsibility. Many do so without recognition, through everyday decisions that shape careers, workplaces and opportunities for others.

Our industry has something extraordinary in common: a purpose that goes far beyond individual careers or commercial success. We are working towards a more sustainable, secure and resilient energy future. And that shared ambition gives us powerful common ground to rethink not only how we produce energy, but how we work together.

According to recent reports, gender equality is sometimes presented as a competition between women and men, as though creating opportunities for one group necessarily means taking something away from another. Yet the experiences shared throughout our Women in Solar+ Europe series suggest a different reality. Inclusion is about removing limitations, not creating newly introduced ones, and allowing people to contribute according to their abilities rather than expectations attached to their gender.

Recent findings suggest that antonio Arruebo, Senior Market Analyst at SolarPower Europe, captured this perspective in our previous reflections on gender equality: “Gender equality liberates everyone.” His message challenges us to recognise that stereotypes restrict men too, particularly when leadership is associated with authority, certainty or emotional restraint. Creating more inclusive workplaces also creates space for men to lead differently, express vulnerability and develop their own potential.

It has been revealed that this is an important conversation for an industry that needs increasingly diverse capabilities. Technical expertise remains essential, but so do empathy, collaboration, adaptability and the ability to bring people together around complex challenges. None of these qualities belongs exclusively to one gender.

Sources indicate that progress also requires the courage to acknowledge that none of us is free from bias. We all develop assumptions through our upbringing, education and professional experiences. What matters is whether we are willing to recognise them and reconsider how they influence our decisions.

Sources indicate that emiliano Bellini, News Director at pv magazine, explored this in his contribution to our series, encouraging open conversations and greater tolerance for mistakes when addressing unconscious bias. His message was clear: “We must free our thinking and allow room for mistakes.”.

This is particularly relevant when engaging more men in conversations about inclusion. Fear of saying the wrong thing should not prevent participation. We need environments where people can ask questions, disagree respectfully, learn from different perspectives and evolve together. Inclusion cannot flourish if conversations become another space where people feel judged rather than encouraged to grow.

Of course, positive intentions must translate into action. The real test of inclusive leadership comes through everyday decisions about recruitment, recognition, promotion and professional development.

Recent findings suggest that josef Kastner, CEO of Nexun, addressed this responsibility in his contribution to the series, highlighting how conscious and unconscious bias influences career opportunities. His position was unequivocal: “Everyone deserves the same rights and opportunities.” Kastner also shared how he challenged inappropriate behaviour towards a female manager, demonstrating that allyship is not simply about supporting equality in principle. It means being prepared to act when fairness is compromised, even when those conversations are uncomfortable.

Frank Niendorf, Vice President Europe at JinkoSolar, offered a complementary perspective on the evolution of leadership and the importance of creating inclusive working environments. He highlighted that effective leadership goes beyond traditional notions of authority and assertiveness. It is about fostering open dialogue, listening actively and encouraging diverse perspectives, ensuring that everyone feels empowered to contribute. His perspective reinforces how challenging conventional leadership stereotypes can help create stronger, more collaborative teams.

This conversation feels particularly relevant during Movember, a global movement raising awareness of men’s mental and physical health, including mental health and suicide prevention, prostate cancer and testicular cancer. In industries like ours, where demanding targets, constant change and high levels of responsibility are part of everyday life, we should also question the expectations placed on men to always appear strong, confident and in control. Creating psychologically safe workplaces means ensuring that men, too, feel comfortable expressing vulnerability, asking for support and speaking openly about their wellbeing. An inclusive culture should not only help women overcome the barriers they face; it should also help men overcome the expectations that hold them back.

These reflections matter because organisational cultures are shaped by what leaders encourage, tolerate and challenge. The men who question their own assumptions, sponsor emerging talent, share recognition and create opportunities for others contribute directly to building stronger, more capable teams.

In a recent development, the energy transition is often discussed through gigawatts, investment, infrastructure and technological innovation. Yet behind every project are people whose ability to collaborate determines whether those ambitions become reality.

Kim Keats, Partner at Ekon Strategy Consulting, offered a timely reminder in his contribution to our series: “Our industry is ultimately about people, not just technology, models or spreadsheets.”.

His reflections highlighted the importance of trust, meaningful dialogue and listening to perspectives that might otherwise be overlooked. Similarly, Jesús Alijarde, General Director of Ibersyd/Cerfo, emphasised the importance of creating environments where employees feel safe enough to challenge decisions openly. “Showing your team that you do not know everything and that you also make mistakes allows the organisation to grow much faster together,” he explained in our pv magazine series.

Industry observers note that both perspectives point towards a leadership model that values people as individuals rather than simply resources. They also challenge the traditional expectation that leaders, particularly men, must always project certainty and have all the answers. This becomes increasingly important as our industries navigate rapid technological change, growing complexity and the integration of artificial intelligence into everyday work.

Recent findings suggest that at Women in Solar+ Europe, we have always believed that building a more inclusive industry requires women and men working together. We need men who are willing to listen, challenge inherited assumptions and recognise that supporting others does not diminish their own achievements. Equally, we need to create spaces where men can participate authentically, without being reduced to stereotypes or expected to have every answer.

This belief is so central to our mission that it led us to create Solar+ Leaders, our leadership development ecosystem open to everyone across the solar and wider energy transition industries, regardless of gender. Through mentoring, leadership development, shared learning and meaningful connections, we are building a community where people can grow together, challenge their assumptions and develop the human capabilities our industries need to navigate an increasingly complex future.

Because Solar+ Leaders is not a place where we talk about inclusive leadership. It is where we nurture it and put it into practice. And where we recognise that the energy transition is not only a technological challenge; it is a leadership challenge.

Industry observers note that on this International Men’s Day, our message is one of appreciation to the many men who contribute to our industry with integrity, generosity and a genuine desire to make a difference. Those who mentor, encourage, collaborate, open doors and help others discover what they are capable of achieving.

Leadership has no gender; it has values. And perhaps the greatest opportunity before us is to build an industry where those values allow everyone to thrive.

Because the energy transition is not a competition between women and men. It is a collective mission that needs the very best of all of us.

It has been revealed that interested in connecting with other women leaders and experts across the solar and wider energy transition industries? Join Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) at www.wiseu.network. Or explore Solar+ Leaders, our inclusive leadership development ecosystem open to everyone, regardless of gender, where we nurture and practise human-centred leadership through mentoring, shared learning and meaningful connections. Find out more at www.solarplusleaders.com.

The views and opinions expressed in this article are the author’s own, and do not necessarily reflect those held by pv magazine.

#618. CATL, BYD, ACWA among co-initiators of storage alliance unveiled at COP31

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (451 w)
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pv-magazine

CATL, BYD, ACWA among co-initiators of storage alliance unveiled at COP31

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (451 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pv-magazine

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Global Energy Storage Alliance, known as GESA, was debuted on Nov.
  • The three founding organizations are the China Energy Storage Alliance, the China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute, and China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage Co.
  • The launch event was attended by Liu Zhenmin, China’s Special Envoy for Climate Change; Francesco La Camera, Director-General of the International Renewable Energy Agency; Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of ESCAP; and Xiong Minfeng, Deputy Director-General of the International Cooperation Department at China’s National Energy Administration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Global Energy Storage Alliance, known as GESA, was debuted on Nov. 13 at the China Pavilion during COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, bringing together 27 co-initiating organizations spanning battery manufacturers, power utilities, state-owned enterprises, and research institutions from China and several other countries.

The three founding organizations are the China Energy Storage Alliance, the China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute, and China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage Co. The co-initiator list includes battery and system manufacturers such as CATL, BYD Energy Storage, EVE Energy, Hithium, and Sungrow, alongside state-owned energy groups including CGN Energy International and POWERCHINA International. Saudi Arabian utility developer ACWA Power is among the international co-initiators. Seven organizations — including the Long Duration Energy Storage Council, the International Hydropower Association, Energy Storage Europe, and the World Resources Institute are listed as interested in exploring participation in GESA.

The launch event was attended by Liu Zhenmin, China’s Special Envoy for Climate Change; Francesco La Camera, Director-General of the International Renewable Energy Agency; Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of ESCAP; and Xiong Minfeng, Deputy Director-General of the International Cooperation Department at China’s National Energy Administration.

GESA’s founding declaration outlines six areas of focus: facilitating international dialogue, building a global storage project and standards database, supporting research and technology deployment, improving market mechanisms, strengthening supply chains and trade, and mobilizing investment for projects in developing economies. The initiative describes itself as open, technology-neutral, and market-oriented, and states it will respect different national regulatory models.

In a recent development, speaking at the launch, Sun Liqun, Deputy General Manager of China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage, identified three structural barriers the initiative aims to address: inadequate market mechanisms for valuing both short- and long-duration storage, fragmented technical standards and regulatory frameworks across countries, and financing and development barriers in emerging economies. These are widely recognized constraints on storage deployment. However, how the degree to which a voluntary industry alliance can move them will depend on the engagement it obtains beyond the launch.

Beyond industry coordination, the alliance carries weight in the UN-led climate process. Storage underpins the global push to triple renewable capacity by 2030, and GESA’s focus on technical assistance, capacity building and de-risked financing for developing economies speaks directly to the Paris Agreement’s call for an equitable transition. By channeling South-South cooperation toward emerging markets in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Latin America, where financing costs remain the biggest obstacle to deployment, the initiative could help narrow the energy access gap between developed and developing countries.

For China, it marks a step from exporting storage products toward shaping global standards, extending its climate diplomacy from setting targets to building a system that deliver them.

#617. Industry News: How to use your phone if the grid goes down

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (909 w)
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci

Industry News: How to use your phone if the grid goes down

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You probably don’t need reminding about our intense reliance on our phones for communication—so what happens when the networks that those phones rely on go down?
  • There are options available to you though, both in terms of what you can do on your phone, and what you can use instead of it.
  • Power outages can be different in scope and type, but for the purposes of this guide we’ll imagine a localized power grid collapse that has knocked out your Wi-Fi router and your local cell tower—but not a global shutdown that’s taken out all infrastructure, including the ground stations communicating with satellites in orbit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You probably don’t need reminding about our intense reliance on our phones for communication—so what happens when the networks that those phones rely on go down? Power and tech outages continue to cause disruptions, and that can leave you stuck when it comes to staying in touch with others.

There are options available to you though, both in terms of what you can do on your phone, and what you can use instead of it. You’ll need to make sure the people you’re chatting with have set up the same options, so it’s worth mentioning at the next family or friends gathering.

Power outages can be different in scope and type, but for the purposes of this guide we’ll imagine a localized power grid collapse that has knocked out your Wi-Fi router and your local cell tower—but not a global shutdown that’s taken out all infrastructure, including the ground stations communicating with satellites in orbit.

Sources indicate that if you’ve acquired a phone from Apple, Samsung, or Google in the last two or three years, it comes with satellite communications built in, so you can still text friends and family if the cell towers go out (calling isn’t an option, due to bandwidth). The feature should kick in automatically in Messages on iOS, or in Google Messages on Android, provided your carrier supports it—you’ll just see a prompt on screen.

Industry observers note that follow the instructions to find a satellite and start texting. There’s nothing to enable or turn on, but if you want to test it out beforehand so you know it works, open Settings then pick Apps > Messages > Satellite Connection Demo (iOS), or Safety and emergency > Satellite SOS (Android).

There is another option on your phone, which is to try a peer-to-peer messaging app. These apps need to be downloaded in advance and work over Bluetooth to send messages in a mesh created by the devices themselves. That means a limited range, but you don’t need any Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity.

One of the best apps in this category is Bridgefy, which you can get for Android and iOS. It’s free to use, simple to operate, and has a range of around 100 meters (or 330 feet). You don’t have to wait until the power goes out to use it either, because you could set up a mesh chat when you’re out camping, or taking a trip with family.

Sources indicate that unless you do a lot of outdoor, off-grid adventuring, you might not have realized just how many devices now exist that can keep you connected even without access to Wi-Fi or cellular networks. Some of these options work via the same satellite networks as your phone.

Recent findings suggest that have a look at the Garmin InReach Messenger Plus, for example, a $299.99 communicator you can use whenever cell networks are down (or just out of range). You’re also going to need an active subscription. They start at $7.99 a month, but once you’re set up you can connect to the wider world from just about anywhere.

According to recent reports, then there are the more straightforward walkie-talkie devices, which operate over radio signals across a range of a few miles. That might just be enough if you’ve got friends and family you need to contact when the power’s out. There are plenty of devices to choose between, but the Motorola T802 Talkabout is a good example and under $100 for a pair.

In a recent development, don’t forget a battery-powered radio either. It won’t let you message anyone directly, but it will mean you can stay up to date with what’s happening out there in the world, and it might give you an idea of when the power’s going to come back on. You can even get models that work via solar or hand-crank power, like this $30 emergency radio.

All of your phones and other devices will need power if they’re going to keep you in touch with other people—otherwise you’ll be relying on smoke signals and postal couriers. So it’s wise to invest in a portable power station ahead of time. Something like the $289 Jackery Explorer 300 would do the job.

Recent findings suggest that obviously you’re going to want to charge up these hefty power stations before the electricity gets cut, otherwise they won’t be much use. But you’re actually not as reliant on the power grid as you might think. Many models (including those offered by Jackery) have solar panel add-ons you can invest in as well.

Even with a backup supply in place, it’s a good idea to try and conserve power on your gadgets as much as possible too. Your phones, tablets, and laptops will all have low power settings you can make use of, but there are standard tips that apply across just about every gadget. Reduce screen brightness and volume as much as possible, and enable airplane mode where you can.

In a recent development, when you do have power and Wi-Fi available, make sure you download as much essential info to your phone as you can, so it’s still there when an internet connection isn’t. This is particularly useful for maps: Both Google Maps (Settings > Offline maps) and Apple Maps (Profile picture > Offline maps) let you do this.

The Exhibition Artifact (Artefacto Expositivo) arose from a commission to build a temporary support to exhibit architectural models developed by students of the UNIACC School of Architecture during a celebration of the academic community. #614. 30+ editor-approved practical gifts for 2026

30+ editor-approved practical gifts for 2026

📅 01 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in my eyes, the best gift is a practical one. It’s useful and won’t rot in the back of someone’s closet for years; they’ll think of you whenever they use it; and you get major brownie points for introducing a magical, miracle product into their life. And what’s better than being known as someone who reliably gifts reliable products? I may still get made fun of by family for my history of wanting practical gifts (including lead refills for my mechanical pencil), but the gifts I treasure most often get the most use in my home. These are some of the best practical gear you can give to friends and family members who value utilitarianism over flash and fluff.

The OLIGHT Baton4 Pro rechargeable flashlight is a $63 flashlight that’s well worth the cost. They’ll never need another flashlight, and they’ll struggle to find one as bright and powerful as this. This torch clocks in at 1600 lumens, and its beam reaches 200 meters long, with a cool white color that cuts through the darkest sky. Dual switches—a side switch and tail switch—allow for one-handed mode selection (choose from high, turbo, and momentary on). Use it hands-free with an included L stand that sticks to metal surfaces, and know it will stay cool and comfortable in hand, even in Turbo mode. Charge it with the included magnetic charger, or unscrew the tailcap to reveal a USB-C port for universal charging anywhere. Your next power outage, camping trip, and attic exploration mission will thank you for this gift.

Carry an entire box’s worth of tools in your hand with this $130 LEATHERMAN Wave Plus 18-in-1 Multi-Tool. Standouts and crowd-pleasers include regular pliers, needle-nose pliers, replaceable wire cutters, knives, a saw, a can opener, a bottle opener, spring-action scissors, and three driver sizes. This multitool is made to be portable, reliable, durable, and multifunctional, all ingredients for one practical gift.

Made from 100 percent Greek Koroneiki olives, this single-varietal, cold-extracted, early harvest extra virgin olive oil adds zest to whatever you love best. From a bowl of simple greens to artisan bread, grilled fish to wood-fired vegetables, you’ll love the grassy, sassy brightness it brings. And that’s how you also know it’s packed with plenty of polyphenols, so you can fight free radicals—reducing inflammation while elevating taste. Combine it with basil and black olives for the kind of flavor the foodies in your life will want to put on a pedestal (not included) … just one of the many kitchen gifts we can recommend.

Being backstage at a show is a vibe. Sometimes weird, sometimes wild, but always an interesting mix of calm and chaos. Chicago’s FRET12 brand aims to capture the smell of decompression and anticipation and bring it home with its hand-poured “Green Room” candle, which blends birch, bark, fig, and bergamot into something restful and ripe you can gift the joint audiophile-aromaphile in your orbit. For something more after-hours and intimate, try “Deep Cuts,” or spark up “Campfire Acoustic” and bask in wafts of sweet, warm smoke and vanilla. Available in 3-, 8-, and 10-ounce sizes. And while you’re at it, pick up a custom-designed and -printed T-shirt and other garb for that special member of your personal road crew who wants to celebrate their love of all things analog while they shop for some M&M’s (no brown ones) and white tube socks. And there’s artwork and actual guitar stuff, too, for gigging musicians!

It has been revealed that the Mileseey GeneSonic Pro and GenePro G1 give you what you want for a casual round with friends, and what you need if you still want to know that carry number or feel confident before you even swing a club in more serious competition. The IP65 GenePro G1 delivers accuracy on par with top-of-the-line rangefinders on the market today, while also giving you a full view of the hole. It offers front/center/back yardages, Ball-to-Pin distance, 600-yard flag-lock, SmartSlope compensation, and more. And the IP67 magnetically mounted GeneSonic Pro speaker delivers quality sound and a built-in detachable GPS with 43,000+ preloaded advanced course views for those pesky cart path-only days. Plus, it’s a 30W power bank, so you can get out and continue to jam out, no matter what the weather brings or how you swing. Whichever one suits your game, you can’t go wrong, and they make a great gift for the golfer in your life.

In a recent development, if you’re looking to give a gift that no one asks for but nearly everybody needs, four fresh tires is something someone you know has been putting off. If you know someone with a pickup, SUV, or van that is constantly on the road in mixed conditions, including snow, you can show you care about their safety with four Kumho Road Venture HT tires [left, above]. They come with a 75,000-mile tread warranty on passenger sizes (50,000 on LT sizes), so this is something they won’t have to think about again for years. The zig-zag tread and 3D interlocking sipes earn these a Three-Peak Mountain Snowflake, which means they beat a standard tire’s acceleration on medium-packed snow by at least 10 percent. Meanwhile, four deep grooves channel water away when rain is the bigger problem, and staggered tread blocks mean less highway hum in general. If you know a driver going everywhere (except off-road), you’ll be giving them smoother rides on a road trip, fewer white-knuckle mornings (even in January), and no tire talk for a while. Having taken them out on a closed course near Seattle, we can confirm good dry grip, even during aggressive cornering, and well-composed wet performance. No, they might not unwrap these and squeal … but with fresh tread, these tires shouldn’t squeal either, and that’s something to get excited about. If the person you’re gifting is an SUV or crossover driver more interested in a quiet, plush ride over snow grip, the Crugen GT Pro [right, above], packed with resonance-reduction tech, offers less wheel slip under hard acceleration, strong hydroplaning resistance, and consistent cabin quietness compared to whatever bald rubber they’ve been riding on for too long.

I’ve sung the praises of this $98 Levoit Core300-P air purifier for years. It’s one of our best budget air purifiers, and there are right now two of them in my home: one in the primary bedroom and another in the living room. The replaceable filters aren’t prohibitively expensive, and they’re whisper-quiet at their lowest speeds. I’ve tested many air purifiers, and this one easily beats its more expensive competitors. My asthmatic cat loves this air purifier, my fiancé, who hasn’t gotten sick in years, loves it, and I love it. I’d buy it for all my friends if I could.

Good things come in small packages, including this $180 Midea dehumidifier, which is two feet high and a little over a foot wide. This small dehumidifier holds 3.2 gallons of water and can cover 1,500 square feet, making it perfect for apartments, bathrooms, and even damp walk-in closets. Control it via app or voice, or use the built-in buttons. A side window indicates when it’s time to empty the water tank, and a handle makes it easy to carry. The dehumidifier is also on wheels, so you don’t even have to carry it in some cases.

Other humidifiers promptly get gross and grody. The Carepod One is a splurge at $279, but this high-end humidifier stays mold-free thanks to a sterilizable, dishwasher-safe stainless steel basin. It has only three parts to clean: the white wand, stainless steel water tank, and stainless steel inner lid. The humidifier runs for up to 30 hours and includes a built-in timer for hassle-free use. It’s Restriction of Hazardous Substances-certified, meaning it’s free of hazardous substances like lead and mercury.

Sometimes, a mess isn’t messy enough to warrant breaking out the big, heavy vacuum, and there is no other pleasure like having a tool for a very specific task. This $80 handheld vacuum from Shark is excellent for cleaning pet hair off couches or collecting the crust from your car. An extra-large dust cup means you can clean all these small messes in one go or have extra room for pet hair when the couch gets particularly fuzzy.

Regardless of water bottle allegiance, the $20 Kuppy Silicone Water Bottle Drying Rack helps reusable bottles of all sizes, wine glasses, and even silicone snack bags dry thoroughly to prevent odor from trapped water. They’re stackable for storage in the water bottle section of a kitchen (Everyone has a Water Bottle Kingdom somewhere in their home). Best of all, they take up less space than traditional dish racks.

Sources indicate that this $37 Aquabliss SF100 Daily Revitalize Shower Filter is for the person in your life who has a codependent relationship with their Brita pitcher. This budget shower filter fits standard fittings and works with fixed, rain, handheld, and combination shower heads. It also adds three to four inches to an existing shower arm and maintains water pressure for cleaner water without weaker streams. The filter cartridge takes two minutes to replace and lasts three to six months depending on water quality.

Industry observers note that the Philips Sonicare Prestige 9900 is a $380 rechargeable toothbrush that provides dentist-level cleaning every day. Sonic technology and multi-angle bristles remove plaque regardless of brush technique. SenseIQ Technology automatically adjusts intensity and flashes when it detects too much pressure. This toothbrush comes with five modes, plus three intensity levels. The Oral-B iO Series 3 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush is a cheaper option that’s still just as giftable.

According to recent reports, A water flosser is the bedrock of a well-rounded oral care routine. The Waterpik Aquarius Countertop Water Flosser is a $100 countertop water flosser that’s more like a power washer for mouths. Choose from 10 settings for extra pearly whites, including a massage mode that helps stimulate gums. Although it’s not a replacement for floss, it’s excellent for getting the job done after a late night. I personally use mine after flossing and add a bit of mouthwash to the reservoir to get fluoride where my teeth need it most.

In a recent development, the Nori Press Travel Steam Iron is a $120 handheld iron that resembles a giant hair straightener. If your gift recipient is like me and has ironed out my polo collars with a hair straightener, this iron should feel familiar. Two heated plates iron the front and back of a garment at once, removing wrinkles without an ironing board. The compact iron also includes a built-in steamer to remove wrinkles from more delicate fabrics. At 14 inches long and weighing a little under 1.5 pounds, it’s packable for clothing emergencies.

The Dyson Supersonic Nural Hair Dryer is a $450 hair dryer designed to maintain healthy hair and a healthy scalp. It’s also engineered to reduce flakes and shedding and balance hair oils. This smart hair dryer reduces airflow and deactivates the heater when set down; a Hall sensor recognizes each attachment as it’s used and automatically adjusts settings based on the attachment; and intelligent heat control monitors airflow to prevent hair damage. It also dries hair fast, a plus for practical friends who hate going to bed with wet hair.

Sources indicate that your most practical friend is most likely a Virgo or Capricorn. Popular Science’s resident Virgo and Managing Editor, Gear & Commerce, enjoys using this Baldscaper to keep his head smooth without causing physical/emotional damage to himself and his loved ones. Four floating shaver heads contour to the head, face, and body for a smooth shave, cutting it close sans nicks and razor burn. It’s fully waterproof, rinses clean with just water, and can be used wet or dry. A powerful motor and 90-minute battery life cut through coarse hair without dying halfway through a head shave.

The TUSHY Classic 3.0 Bidet is a $124 starter bidet that helps your gift recipient feel cleaner than using toilet paper alone. It includes all materials needed for installation, which takes less than 10 minutes. A Schmutz Shield (actual name for this feature) blocks grime from escaping past the toilet lid, and a self-cleaning nozzle means this bidet won’t cause more cleaning-related headaches your practical friend may experience daily.

Shark makes some of the best cordless vacuums, and this $380 option includes some of our favorite features in a vacuum cleaner, including a MultiFLEX wand that makes it infinitely easier to reach under furniture, a light that reveals missed spots, and Floor Detect technology that adjusts brushroll speed depending on the surface. It also doubles as a handvac and comes with tools for crevices and upholstery. With 50 minutes of runtime, HEPA filtration, and an anti-allergen seal, dust busting won’t involve a sneezing fit.

Sources indicate that give the gift of a fully connected home with the $130 Aeotec Smart Home Hub2, which can be used as a SmartThings Hub and supports Zigbee and Matter Gateway protocols. It’s also compatible with Alexa, Google Assistant, and Wi-Fi. Although it’s not Z-Wave compliant, it offers wider device compatibility and stronger security than some competitors.

In a recent development, the best electric blankets provide warmth without turning up the thermostat. This $50 electric throw blanket from Westinghouse is reliable and heats evenly. Plus, it protects itself from overheating and includes an auto-off function for peace of mind when a nap strikes. A weighty smart digital controller cycles through six heat settings and a timer up to 10 hours. Throw it in the washing machine and hang it to dry between seasons.

The Rumpl Gametime Puffy is a $100 2-in-1 stadium accessory made for overtime, any time. It packs a full-size 50×70″ insulated blanket into a TPU-laminated storage case featuring an adjustable, removable shoulder strap and an integrated 1-inch insulated foam pad to sit on when you pull the blanket out (and it’s an extra-padded 4” cushion with the blanket in). The shell and case have a PFAS-free water-repellent finish, and the blanket keeps you warm down to 45 degrees, making it great for football games, soccer matches, and club tournaments.

In a recent development, I’ve assembled my fair share of furniture from a multinational home furnishings store, and let’s be real: Sometimes those Allen wrenches don’t cut it. Enter the Greenworks Pro PowerAll 24V Drill Driver and Impact Driver Combo Kit, a $169 bundle that gives you two handy tools for the price of one. The drill driver and impact driver use brushless motors and 24-volt batteries, and run 20% longer than 18- and 20-volt counterparts. It’s compact, lightweight, and easy to use in tight spaces, making it an excellent gift for DIY-minded friends and family.

The $65 Anyday 4-Piece Medium Glass Food Storage system is made for microwaving or cooking directly in the oven, thanks to sturdy borosilicate glass that’s stronger and better resists extreme temperature changes than soft glass. The glass dishware is even freezer-safe. A glass lid prevents splatters in the microwave; lay-flat knobs vent food while cooking or create an airtight seal when it’s time to store any leftovers.

It has been revealed that this $160 waterproof, compact carry-all from RUX works like an everyday tote, then converts to a roll-top dry bag to protect against rain and random liquids. It fits a laptop, lunch, and any layers, while internal and external pockets keep keys, a phone, and wallet within reach. Grab it by the handles, or wear it crossbody with the included shoulder strap on a two-hands kind of day. Exterior lash points connect pockets and panels (sold separately) for added storage and organization if your gift recipient desires a gift that keeps on giving.

Industry observers note that practical people definitely have plenty of pen opinions—I know I do. And this $6.50 pack of uniball Jetstream pens is a favorite thanks to its smooth, opaque, quick-drying ink that’s water- and fade-resistant. Choose the .7 millimeter option for a finer line, or the 1 millimeter thickness for those who prefer a more robust script.

Sources indicate that my $26 LEUCHTTURM1917 A5 notebook holds my journal ramblings, my to-do lists, and random neurotic notes I need to get out of my head and onto a page. Numbered pages, two page markers, and a blank table of contents help organize all my jumbled thoughts. I personally go for a hardcover notebook with ruled paper, but LEUCHTTURM1917 also sells softcover journals in every color of the rainbow, with square grid ruling, dotted ruling, or blank pages.

Sources indicate that the Ember Mug 3 is the latest generation of the popular smart mug that can keep hot drinks at a precise temperature all day long. Each 14 oz mug includes a sliding lid that extends battery life up to three hours on a single charge (it’s 80 minutes without the lid). And a charging coaster recharges your mug after your daily dose of bean juice (or maintains the temperature indefinitely if you keep the mug on it). Customize your preferred temperature in the app, or set it manually with a button on the mug. It’s also top-rack dishwasher safe.

In a recent development, this $35 leakproof travel mug from BrüMate is for those who don’t mix their coffee with their electronics. A ceramic lining preserves flavor while preventing staining and leftover odors, and triple insulation keeps drinks hot or cold for hours. It’s cup-holder friendly for caffeinating on the go, and a magnetic, OctaLock lid prevents spills while running errands.

It has been revealed that the Click & Carry Ergonomic Grocery Bag Carrier Handle & Bag Holder is a $14 gizmo that saves trips and reduces hassle when unloading groceries. It’s gentle on joints, reduces hand strain, and its ergonomic design lowers injury risk. The bag carrier has a 100-pound weight capacity but weighs just under three ounces. The friend who always tests the boundaries of bringing everything inside in one trip will thank you.

Socks are a well-liked practical gift, and this $25 two-pack of merino wool, COOLMAX EcoMade polyester, REPREVE recycled polyester + nylon socks from Gordini uses fine-gauge and ultra-lightweight yarns to keep feet dry and supported with Linear Wicking Channels that move away moisture and Quilted AirForms that distribute shock and cushion impact. These OrbitFit anatomically mapped 3D zones create a purpose-knit performance fit that keeps you comfortable at home, on a walk, or while running or hiking. If cotton socks are on the gift list, we’re fans of the HUE Women’s Mini Crew Sock and the Men’s Casual Ribbed Crew Socks, which are breathable and comfortable.

The Garmin Venu 4 is a $550 multisport watch that blends style and function. A bright 1.4-inch AMOLED display clearly indicates health and fitness stats like sleep tracking and time needed for workout recovery, along with on-screen workouts. A smart wake alarm helps with waking up at an optimal time, and a built-in LED flashlight illuminates dark morning walks. This watch supports running and triathlon, strength training, jet lag recovery, and more. Data-obsessed friends and family members will be pleased with all the numbers and stats they can pull from this watch.

This $50 OtterBox Symmetry Series Case has protected my iPhone 13 for years: the only blemish is a dent in the aluminum bumper from when I took it out of its case and immediately dropped it on my concrete porch. I’ve learned my lesson and never forgo a phone case. The OtterBox Symmetry Series Case is sleek without being too flimsy and protects without bulk. It’s on my repurchase list and should be on yours, too, especially if you’re looking at one of the upcoming iPhone 18s.

Sources indicate that these newly refreshed noise-canceling headphones from Bose are essential for quiet commutes and tuning out the airport chaos while traveling. Bose makes some of our favorite noise-canceling headphones and earbuds thanks to thoughtful design and helpful tech in each pair. We’re particularly fond of the comfortable pill-shaped earcups, 24-hour battery life, Immersive Audio, QuietControl noise cancellation, and updated ActiveSense Tech to smooth sound spikes in Aware Mode.

According to recent reports, this practical gift is also personal. Every pair of these $249 orthotics from Stride is custom-made from a 3D scan of someone’s foot and a gait video with just their smartphone required, no doctor’s visit necessary. Take a short quiz about pain areas, activity levels, goals, and shoe preferences; provide the digital data; and podiatrists in Germany customize the orthotics and print them on durable TPU (personalized for the recipient) before they arrive at your doorstep in just 10 to 15 days. And they go well beyond arch support. It’s hard to convey the initially odd and then quickly invigorating sensation of an insole that considers each unique contour of the ball of your foot, but we guarantee your achiest friend or family member will appreciate a custom gift that addresses a substantial pain point, literally.

I hate when gloves hinder my range of movement. These $85 bike gloves from Hestra have a flexible but durable outer fabric and stretchy polyester on the palm. Primaloft Gold synthetic insulation, a fleece lining, and a membrane that stops rain and slush without making hands clammy keep your fingers warm. And the Lycra-clad slit makes the glove easy to put on and take off. Even if we don’t ride, these gloves could be our ride or die.

Style and practicality can go hand-in-hand. The Danner Chelsea boot is just that: Proudly assembled in the company’s Portland, Oregon factory with signature stitchdown construction, it slips on and is made of full-grain leather. The nonconductive (Electrical Hazard Certified) outsole is oil- and slip-resistant and is comfortable and durable even after climbing on ladders or standing on unforgiving surfaces like wood, tile, or concrete. Even better, the boots are Danner Recraftable, meaning they are eligible for part replacements, leather care, and restitching (paid services), so you are investing in someone’s ongoing comfort. If your gift recipient is good with laces, the Bull Run Moc Toe is another top choice for both looks and stability.

These $249 Nike slides are a collab with recovery tech giant Hyperice, known for its wellness and recovery technology (we’re presently testing the Normatec dynamic air compression massage legs to positive effect). The comfortable slides combine heat, vibration, and responsive cushioning to make every step feel lighter. They’re like giving a pair of heated slippers a friar-like tonsure.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a woman in your life who carries the world on their shoulders. They shouldn’t have to carry back pain, too. Maybe you’ve heard about Taylor Swift’s posture-correcting bra, or maybe you’ve just listened to a busty friend (or your mom) complain that her back feels like a janky Jenga stack of crooked vertebrae. Is this nearly $200 bra worth it? In a word: absolutely. Designed in seven sizes, up to a G cup, this FDA-registered posture corrector looks like a high-necked crop top with extra-wide straps and a mesh front panel. It gently pulls shoulders into alignment and hugs the girls with serious support—fair warning, though: it can be a wrestling match to get it on and off at first. This one’s more for workouts or lounging at home than for a lift-and-separate situation. Still, it can battle desk-job hunch and is a major relief from digging bra straps.

Industry observers note that know somebody in your family who says “I’m just a little stiff!” while grimacing as they ease down the stairs after pickleball? Then you know someone who would appreciate the gift of some McDavid support. For instance, the $56.99 NRG above wraps polymer springs on each side of the knee for energy return, while taking up to 12.5 percent stress off each knee. And if that someone you know if coming back from something more serious than soreness, there are slip-on neoprene sleeves for stability all the way to braces that add Maximum+ support, for serious rehab, once you go up to the hinged Bio-Logix line. And once someone is back to throwing their body around, they could appreciate the HEX padded sleeves and compression tights. Brand ambassador Kyrie Irving vouches for them after a torn ACL. And since McDavid has gear that is HSA/FSA-eligible, you can treat yourself to fatigue relief, too, if you’ve got some use-it-or-lose-it dollars left at the end of 2026.

Just because you see a jacket that you feel suits you doesn’t always mean it fits you. The same goes for folks on your gift list. But there’s an alternative to something off-the-rack that’s right in the shoulders but maybe tight in the hips. Maybe the sleeves are right, but it only works if you don’t zip it. Or maybe it’s only available in cost-prohibitive heirloom hides. Well, the Jacket Maker will cut a style to the wearer’s own measurements, and every measurement in their guide comes with a how-to video to make sure you get it right. The team also checks numbers against standard sizing and clarifies/suggests alterations if anything stands out. After that, decisions come down to the customer, from the leather and lining to adding embroidery or emblems, and choosing different shades of hardware. Once completed and pictures are approved, which can take 5-7 weeks, it’s shipped worldwide for free, with duties included at checkout. Sure, gifting at Christmas means they’ll be wearing it in spring, but there’s a thrill in the customization and anticipation and finally seeing them actually reach for that favorite jacket every time they head toward the door. It’ll give you and them a warm, fuzzy feeling … literally, with the right liner. (And there are plentiful ready-to-wear styles, too, if that’s more your jam.).

It has been revealed that the Rode NT1 Signature Series is a $159 workhorse. This cardioid condenser microphone has warm bass, a detailed midrange, and glistening highs for exceptional performance when recording bedroom melodies and harmonies, instruments, voiceovers, and a podcast episode that may never see the sun. Choose from eight vibrant colors, including red, green, blue, cobalt, and orange, or stick with black. Keep us updated on the views and streams! And if you’re looking for an extremely versatile mic and willing to pay a little more, the AKG C114 Large Diaphragm Multi-Pattern Condenser Microphone is a 2026 release we’ve seen used to record an entire band to a greatly immersive effect.

Gifting gear or a gadget related to someone’s hobby will always be a hit. If someone in your life recently got an acoustic guitar, a clip-on tuner is a present that keeps giving. This high-precision tuner blocks room noise for faster, easier tuning. Strummed chords ring out in tune, and songs sound infinitely better for it. If an electric guitar and a pedalboard are part of the gear setup, consider adding a tuner pedal like the TC Electronic POLYTUNE 3.

It has been revealed that after many frigid Pittsburgh winters, I’ve learned that investing in a down jacket always pays off. I’m a fan of Stio’s $449 Colter Down Jacket, but the Hometown style is an even more budget-friendly down jacket. A recycled nylon ripstop outer with a PFAS-free DWR shields from the elements. It’s insulated with HyperDRY water-repellent goose down that offers 800-fill warmth even in wet snow. Other helpful features include pockets for hand warmers and valuable tech, and low-profile cord locks for a customized fit. We also think this limited-edition anniversary denim print shown above is just darling.
